# SMK Test Board

A 3×3 macropad built around the Seeed XIAO ESP32-C6, with a rotary encoder and
per-key RGB. It exists to validate the [SMK](https://github.com/mburger89/SMK)
keyboard firmware and the
[SMK Configurator](https://github.com/mburger89/smk_configurator) editor on real
hardware — small enough to be cheap, complete enough to exercise every subsystem
the full keyboard depends on.

Two of those subsystems have never run against physical hardware at all: the RMT
LED driver and `BatteryMonitor`. This board is where they get their first test.

**The schematic and PCB are generated by a Python script, not drawn by hand.**
`generate_test_board.py` is the source of truth; the files under
`smk_test_board/` are its output and should never be hand-edited.

## Status

Design complete, reviewed, and DRC-clean. **Not yet fabricated.**

Before ordering, `docs/fabrication.md` opens with a STOP gate: two footprints —
`XIAO_ESP32C6_HEADERS` and `EC11_VERTICAL` — were drawn from datasheet
dimensions and have never been checked against real parts. Print the board 1:1
and hold the physical XIAO and EC11 against the paper first. A wrong
castellation pitch or encoder pin spacing is not reworkable; it means a second
fab run.

## What's on it

| | |
|---|---|
| MCU | Seeed XIAO ESP32-C6 on 1×7 female headers |
| Matrix | 3×3, 19.05 mm pitch, Gateron KS-33 hot-swap sockets, SOD-123 diodes |
| Encoder | EC11 vertical; its push-switch **is** matrix position row 0, col 2 |
| RGB | 9 × SK6812MINI-E, reverse-mount, one per key, behind an SN74AHCT1G125 level shifter |
| Power | USB-C on the XIAO, or a single-cell Li-ion via JST **SH** (1.0 mm) with flying leads to the module's underside BAT pads |
| Battery sense | External 1:2 divider (2 × 200 kΩ) into GPIO 0 |
| Board | 2-layer, 76.0 × 113.16 mm, 1.6 mm |

The nine LEDs are reverse-mount and shine *through* milled windows in the board
into each switch's north opening. Those windows are internal `Edge.Cuts`
cutouts, not decoration — a fab house that ignores them produces a board whose
LEDs do nothing.

## Pin map

This is a contract shared by four repositories, and all four must agree:

| Signal | GPIO |
|---|---|
| ROW0–2 | 1, 2, 21 |
| COL0–2 | 22, 23, 16 (`colsAreDriven = 1`) |
| LED data | 20 |
| VBAT sense | 0 (ADC1_CH0) |
| Encoder A/B | 17, 19 |

The four places it appears: `generate_test_board.py`'s `PIN` map, the firmware's
`Main.swift`/`Kconfig.projbuild`, the configurator's
`KeyboardDesign.smkTestBoard`, and this repo's `keymap.json`.

**Encoder rotation is not implemented.** GPIO 17/19 are wired and idle — nothing
decodes quadrature yet. That gets its own design once this board physically
exists. The encoder's *push* works, because it is an ordinary matrix position.

The LED chain is wired **serpentine** (even rows left-to-right, odd rows
right-to-left) to match `ledChainIndex()` in the firmware's
`SMKCore/LEDChainMapping.swift`. This is easy to get wrong and invisible when you
do: on a 3×3, raster and serpentine order agree on rows 0 and 2 and differ only
on row 1. `test_led_chain_order_matches_firmwares_serpentine_mapping` checks all
nine positions for exactly that reason.

## Layout

```
generate_test_board.py     the generator — schematic, PCB, placement, netlist
export_fab.py              gerbers, drill files, and the fab zip
test_test_board.py         netlist, placement, and cross-repo contract tests
test_footprints.py         footprint geometry tests
keymap.json                reference keymap (mo:1 on the encoder press)
smk_test_board/            generated KiCad project — do not hand-edit
smk_test_board.pretty/     local footprint library
docs/fabrication.md        BOM, order spec, DRC triage, pre-order gate
docs/bring-up.md           11-step procedure for a delivered board
docs/superpowers/          design spec and implementation plan
```

## Working on it

```bash
python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install pytest
venv/bin/python -m pytest          # 23 tests
python3 generate_test_board.py     # regenerate the KiCad project
python3 export_fab.py              # gerbers + drill + zip into gerbers/
```

Regeneration is byte-reproducible, UUIDs included — so after any change to the
generator, `git diff` on `smk_test_board/` shows exactly what moved
electrically. If you expected a documentation-only change and the `.kicad_pcb`
moved, that is a real finding, not noise.

Fabrication output lands in `gerbers/` and is gitignored. Generate it fresh at
order time rather than trusting a checked-in copy.

## Bringing one up

`docs/bring-up.md` is an ordered checklist with a blank result field per step.
The order matters: continuity checks happen **before** the XIAO is ever seated,
and the battery flying leads get soldered before anything is powered from a
cell.

Two things reliably waste an afternoon if you don't know them, and both are
called out in that document:

- The firmware's board selection defaults to the *other* board. Flash without
  changing it and you get the wrong pin map, and every matrix test fails
  confusingly.
- Two-Mac bonding needs `CONFIG_BT_NIMBLE_MAX_BONDS=4`. With the default of 1,
  the second Mac evicts the first and the test cannot pass.

## Known and accepted

- The board ships **ratsnest-only** — no copper routing. `unconnected_items` in
  DRC is expected and is not something to "fix."
- `min_copper_edge_clearance` is relaxed to 0.2 mm in the project file, because
  the SK6812 pads sit ~0.233–0.247 mm from their own light windows. That is a
  **relaxed rule, not a passing check.** The basis for proceeding is precedent:
  the sibling `smk_kbd_rp2040` board shipped 59 instances of this exact
  footprint at the same clearance.
- RGB3 will be visibly dimmer than the rest — the EC11's body covers roughly the
  southern half of its light window. Expected, not a fault.
- Li-ion cells are commonly sold with a JST-**PH** (2.0 mm) pigtail, which will
  not mate with this board's **SH** (1.0 mm) connector. Source an SH cell, an
  adapter, or re-terminate.
